column2: Third-day entry into Ziklag reveals Amalek's attack on south and city, striking and burning with fire. The repeated city and destructive verbs remain.

Women and everything small to great are introduced before the explicit denial of killing either man or woman and the contrasting captivity and departure. The unusual fronted phrase remains without reversing the stated non-killing.
David's arrival presents the burned city with there it was, and wives, sons and daughters are captives; all family categories remain.
David and men lift their voices and weep until strength for weeping is gone. The repeated weeping and exhausted endpoint remain.
Both wives are named as captives, with Ahinoam's Jezreelite origin and Abigail's identification through Nabal the Carmelite retained.

Propose because to connect the people's talk of stoning David to their anguish over sons and daughters. David's affliction and strengthening in the Lord remain, with collective soul and individual bereavement both expressed.
David asks priest Abiathar son of Ahimelech to bring the ephoud; Ahimelech follows this unit's Greek rather than being harmonized to the book's earlier Abimelech forms.
The questions concern pursuit and overtaking the geddour; the response commands pursuit with emphatic overtaking and rescue. Both certainly expressions are supported by cognate constructions.
column3: Geddour remains an opaque raid-group term rather than an unmarked new military category.

column2: Six hundred men reach the Bosor torrent and remaining men stop. Six hundred is preserved here despite four hundred in earlier chapters.
Four hundred pursue while two hundred stay seated beyond Bosor; both quantities and beyond remain as selected.
An Egyptian is found in a field and brought to David in a field, then given bread and water; repeated location and separate food/drink actions remain.
A fruit-cake portion is eaten and his spirit settles within him after three days and three nights without bread or water. No additional food item is supplied from another text.
column3: Fruit cake for palathe is less specific than the earlier fig-cake rendering; ingredient identification remains a lexical consistency question, not an assumed different recipe.

column2: David asks ownership and origin; the Egyptian youth identifies an Amalekite master and abandonment after illness, today being the third day.
The raid confession names south of Cholthi, Judean regions, south of Cheloub and Ziklag's burning. Selected names are not normalized into ethnic labels without evidence.
Guidance to the geddour is conditioned on an oath against killing or returning the youth to his master. Both protections and repeated destination remain.
The guide reveals people spread over all the land, eating, drinking and celebrating great spoils from both foreign and Judahite lands. There they were carries the presentative.
David strikes from daybreak to evening and the following day; only four hundred camel-mounted youths escape.
column3: The selected time sequence remains without changing daybreak to twilight; the exception's number is not harmonized with the pursuing force.

column2: Everything taken is recovered, with both wives separately rescued. The general recovery does not replace the particular family statement.
Nothing small or great, spoil, sons, daughters or any taken thing is missing; David returns all. The comprehensive categories and repeated all remain.
David leads all flocks and herds before the spoils, which receive the name David's spoils; the naming statement is not given an invented speaker.
The two hundred were too weak and seated by David at Bosor; they meet the returning group and ask David about his welfare. The selected asking direction is not reversed.

The pestilent and evil warriors refuse spoil to non-pursuers, allowing only each wife and children before departure. Only follows the source's explicit exception, and the refusal remains their speech.
David forbids this after the Lord's giving and guarding, repeating divine delivery of the attacking geddour into their hands. The shared divine gift grounds his response.

Propose For before the second explanation: the equal share of fighter and equipment keeper follows their being no less than the others. The question, equality claim and concluding equal division remain.
The practice becomes a command and rule for Israel from that day to today; both normative nouns and full temporal extent remain.
David sends spoil from Ziklag to Judah's elders and his neighbors, presenting it as from the Lord's enemies. Both recipient groups remain.
The list begins with Beth-zur, Ramah of the south and Jeththor; He sent it supplies the continuing action from verse 26 for readable English.
Aroer, the Ammadi, Saphi and Esthie remain in order; the Ammadi are not silently recast as another city's residents.
The full additional stored unit retains recipients in Gath, Kinan, Saphek and Thimath, in the selected position between 28 and 29. It is not merged away or renumbered.
Carmel, the Ierameli cities and Kenezi cities remain, with cities explicit for both latter groups.
Ierimouth, Beer-sheba and Noo remain the next three recipient locations; no map-based corrections are introduced.
Hebron and all places traversed by David and his men close the distribution list. The general inclusion supplements rather than replaces named places.
Foreign attack, Israelite flight and falling wounded on Gelboue remain. Wounded follows traumatiai without assuming every casualty here was dead.
Foreigners close in and strike Jonathan, Aminadab and Melchisa, named as Saul's sons. The selected names remain, with later death confirmed in verse 6.
Battle grows heavy, missile throwers identified as archers find Saul, and he is wounded beneath the ribs. The rib location is not replaced by general severe injury.
column3: The relationship of akontistai and toxotai remains unusual; the appositional English preserves both descriptions without inventing a second troop group.

column2: Saul requests piercing to avoid enemy piercing and mockery; the bearer refuses through fear, and Saul takes the sword and falls on it. The historical violence is translated without extra procedural detail.
The bearer sees Saul dead, falls on his own sword and dies with him; the observed death and subsequent action remain distinct.
Saul, three sons and bearer die together that day; no additional all-his-men clause is imported.
Israelites beyond both valley and Jordan see flight and royal deaths, abandon cities, and foreigners occupy them. Both geographic groups and occupation remain.
On the next day foreigners strip the dead and discover Saul and three sons on plural Gelboue mountains. The plural mountain form remains.
The foreigners turn him over, remove equipment and send it around with news to idols and people. No beheading is supplied where this selected text says turned him over.
column3: Equipment is the antecedent of the plural sent objects; the body is not silently made the distributed object.

column2: Equipment is dedicated in Astarte's temple and the body fastened to Beth-shan's wall. The distinct objects and locations remain.
Jabesh-Gilead's inhabitants hear what was done to Saul, motivating the following recovery without an added speech.
All mighty men travel the entire night and recover Saul's body and specifically Jonathan's body from the wall, bring them to Jabesh and burn them there.
column3: The other sons' bodies are not inserted into the selected two-body statement; the burning is retained without a reconstructed funerary explanation.

column2: Their bones are buried beneath cultivated ground at Jabesh and a seven-day fast follows. Cultivated ground is not replaced by a tree from another witness.
